course.description: Get your machine ready to build real web applications with AI. No coding experience required — just follow the steps and you'll have everything installed and configured by the end.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Vibecoding: Your First Dev Environment Setup.

modules.description: Your workspace is where everything happens. VS Code is the industry standard text editor for developers and the home base for all your vibecoding sessions.

lessons.content:
**What it is:** A text editor designed for code. Think Microsoft Word, but for programming. This is where you'll see your project files and interact with Claude Code.

**Why you need it:** Technically, you could write code in any text editor. But VS Code has a built-in terminal (command line) and thousands of helpful extensions that make your life way easier. It's free, made by Microsoft, and it's what most developers use.

**Installation:**
1. Go to [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com)
2. Click the download button (it detects your operating system automatically)
3. Run the installer

**Verify it worked:** Open VS Code. You should see a welcome screen with some getting-started options.
lessons.title: Install VS Code

modules.title: Code Editor Setup

modules.description: Your computer doesn't natively understand JavaScript. Node.js fixes that — and unlocks the entire ecosystem of modern web development tools.

lessons.content:
**What it is:** Node.js is a "runtime" program that teaches your computer how to read and execute JavaScript code.

**Why you need it:** Easy analogy — you need Word to open a `.docx` file, you need Node.js to run JavaScript. Almost every modern web development tool is built with JavaScript and distributed through npm (Node Package Manager).

**Installation:**
1. Go to [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org)
2. Download the **LTS version** (labeled "Recommended for Most Users")
3. Run the installer and accept all the defaults

**Verify it worked:**
1. Open VS Code
2. Open the terminal: **View → Terminal** (or press `Ctrl+\`` on Windows, `Cmd+\`` on Mac)
3. Type `node --version` and press Enter

You should see a version number like `v24.13.0`. The exact number doesn't matter — what matters is that it shows *something* instead of an error.
lessons.title: Install Node.js

modules.title: JavaScript Runtime

modules.description: Git tracks every change you make to your code. Made a mistake? Undo it. Ready to deploy? Git makes that possible too.

lessons.content:
**What it is:** Git is version control software that tracks every change you make to your code.

**Why you need it:**
- You and Claude Code can rewind to previous versions of your project
- Deployment services like Vercel pull your code directly from GitHub
- Collaborators can access and contribute to your codebase

**Installation:**

*Mac:* Open the terminal in VS Code and type `git --version`. If Git isn't installed, your Mac will prompt you to install the Command Line Developer Tools. Click **Install** and wait a few minutes.

*Windows:* Go to [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com), download the installer, and run it. Accept all the defaults.

**Verify it worked:** Type `git --version` in the terminal. You should see a version number.
lessons.title: Install Git

modules.title: Version Control

modules.description: This is the whole point. Claude Code is the AI assistant that writes, edits, and runs code based on your plain-English instructions.

lessons.content:
**What it is:** Claude Code is an AI coding assistant that runs in your terminal. You tell it what you want to build, and it handles the code. Made by Anthropic, the same company behind Claude.

**Installation:**

Open VS Code's terminal and run the command for your operating system:

*Mac/Linux:*
```
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | sh
```

*Windows PowerShell:*
```
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

Once it finishes, type `claude` to start Claude Code and follow the prompts to authenticate with your Anthropic account.

**Verify it worked:** Type `claude` in the terminal. You should see Claude Code start up and greet you.
lessons.title: Install Claude Code

lessons.content:
Claude Code lets you choose which AI model powers your sessions. Here's how to think about it:

| Model | Best For | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Sonnet** | Day-to-day coding and execution | Standard |
| **Opus** | Planning, architecture, complex decisions | 3x Sonnet |

**Recommended approach:** Use Opus when you're planning what to build. Switch to Sonnet when you're executing and writing code. This gives you the best results without burning through credits unnecessarily.
lessons.title: Understand Your Model Options

modules.title: Claude Code

modules.description: Claude Code is installed — now you need accounts on four services before you can build and deploy real applications.

lessons.content:
Claude Code requires either a **Claude Pro subscription** ($20/month) or API credits.

- Already a Claude Pro subscriber? You're set.
- Not subscribed? Sign up at [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com)
lessons.title: Set Up Anthropic Access

lessons.content:
**What it is:** GitHub is where your code lives in the cloud. Think Google Drive, but for code.

**Why you need it:** Your GitHub repository is the "source of truth" for your project. Deployment services watch it for changes and automatically push updates to your live app.

Sign up at [github.com](https://github.com) and save your username and password — you'll need them in the next step.
lessons.title: Create a GitHub Account

lessons.content:
**What it is:** Vercel hosts your app and gives it a real URL on the internet.

**Why you need it:** When you push code to GitHub, Vercel automatically deploys it. No manual uploading or server management required.

1. Sign up at [vercel.com](https://vercel.com)
2. Use **Continue with GitHub** to link your accounts
lessons.title: Connect Vercel

lessons.content:
**What it is:** Supabase is your database and user authentication platform — the place your app stores and retrieves data.

**Why you need it:** Most real applications need to store data somewhere. Supabase has become the go-to database tool in the vibecoder toolkit.

1. Sign up at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com)
2. Use **Sign in with GitHub** to connect your accounts
lessons.title: Set Up Supabase

modules.title: Account Setup

modules.description: You're set up. Here's everything you should have in place before moving on to building your first app.

lessons.content:
Run through this checklist — every item should be checked before you continue:

- [ ] **VS Code** installed and opens without errors
- [ ] **Node.js** installed — `node --version` returns a version number
- [ ] **Git** installed — `git --version` returns a version number
- [ ] **Claude Code** installed — typing `claude` in the terminal starts a session
- [ ] **Anthropic** account active with Claude Pro or API credits
- [ ] **GitHub** account created
- [ ] **Vercel** account connected to GitHub
- [ ] **Supabase** account connected to GitHub
lessons.title: Confirm Your Setup

lessons.content:
Before you close out, do this right now:

1. Open VS Code
2. Open the terminal
3. Type `claude` and press Enter
4. Say hello

You're a vibecoder now. The next guide walks through building and deploying your first real application — from describing what you want, to generating product documentation, to a live app on the internet.# Vibecoding: Your First Dev Environment Setup
